finding.claim: PUT /doc/<doc_id> lets any caller overwrite any document's body. The can_edit result is discarded, so no authorization check runs before the write.
finding.source: URL doc_id and request.json['body'] on PUT /doc/<doc_id>; caller needs only an authenticated session that sets g.user (populating g.user is outside this repo).

trace.note: can_edit(g.user, doc) called; return value discarded, no abort(403)
Attacker body written to document; handler returns ok=True

finding.guards_checked: can_edit (docs.py:7-8) is correct but unused on this path; require_edit (docs.py:11-13) not called in update_doc; no before_request hook, decorator, or ownership check in file. Title route (docs.py:27) is correctly guarded, confirming omission.

verdict.guard_found: can_edit (docs.py:7-8) is called at docs.py:19 but its bool result is discarded, so it does not block the write. require_edit (docs.py:11-13) is not called in update_doc. No before_request hook, decorator, or ownership check exists in docs.py or any other file in the directory. The only other file, the security-research skill docs under .claude/, is not application code.
verdict.reason: The trace matches the code: docs.py:19 calls can_edit(g.user, doc) as a bare statement, its False result is never tested, and docs.py:20 writes request.json["body"] into doc["body"] unconditionally, so any authenticated user (g.user set, per the candidate's assumption) can overwrite any document's body via PUT /doc/<doc_id>, while the title route at docs.py:27 uses require_edit and correctly aborts.

finding.claim: Missing documents return 500 while unauthorized existing documents return 403 on the title route, letting an attacker enumerate existing doc IDs. Missing g.user yields 500 instead of 401.
finding.source: Arbitrary doc_id in URL on PUT /doc/<doc_id>/title (and body route).
finding.sink: DOCS[doc_id] KeyError at docs.py:26 (and docs.py:18); AttributeError on g.user at docs.py:27 when unset.

trace.note: DOCS[doc_id] raises KeyError for unknown IDs, yielding 500
require_edit reached for existing docs; abort(403) at docs.py:13 when not permitted
403 response only for existing docs, distinguishing them from 500 for missing docs

finding.guards_checked: 403 path in require_edit is correct for authorization; issue is inconsistent error handling for missing IDs and missing identity. Debug mode not set in this file, so no traceback leak shown here.

verdict.guard_found: none blocks the missing-vs-forbidden distinction. require_edit (docs.py:11-13) returns nothing and aborts with 403 only for existing docs, and the unknown-ID path raises KeyError at docs.py:26 before any check runs. Anonymous callers are not a realistic attacker: g.user is unset outside this file, so any request reaches the AttributeError at docs.py:27 and gets a 500 for every ID. The attacker must be an authenticated user for the 500-vs-403 oracle to appear.
verdict.reason: The title route at docs.py:26-27 returns a 500 from the KeyError for unknown IDs and a 403 from docs.py:13 for existing docs the caller cannot edit, so an authenticated user can enumerate document IDs; this is a low-severity info leak, and the missing-g.user 500 at docs.py:27 is a hardening issue rather than a security flaw.
